<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c89754740435dcff4c48f83f371270d4fafaee321bd6c3303e2263e1c070a716"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Filtering leaves GlasgowLive's blocked top billboard as an empty 1000x260 sticky white strip that pushes the site header down 260px and swallows left clicks on headline links beneath it (elementFromPoint at the teaser link returns the strip), matching the reporter's "left click does not navigate". A site-scoped cosmetic rule hiding that leftover strip was visually verified as resolving it with page integrity intact, but the apply_rule environment refused both selector forms, so the rule is attached for a maintainer instead of being proposed.

## Candidate for review

`glasgowlive.co.uk##body > div:has(> .commercial-box-child-style)`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule refused both forms. This one returned baseline_symptom_absent:⁠ the site paints the same emptied billboard wrapper (1000x260, white, position:⁠sticky, z-index 9998, holding .commercial-box-child-style ⁠> .commercial-gpt-style) on the unfiltered page too, only its content differs, so the harness could not separate filtered from unfiltered and ran no visual review. The equivalent glasgowlive.co.uk#⁠#⁠div.sticky:⁠has(⁠> .commercial-box-child-style) did get a bound visual review that verified it (symptom resolved, pageIntegrity intact, adLayoutResidue absent, remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty) but its environmentExperiment failed candidate_phase_symptom, which the contract reads as the symptom still there, so it cannot be carried. The body ⁠> div form is preferred because one observed load applied no sticky class, on which div.sticky matches nothing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42434758286

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.tour.ne.jp the reporter's annotation marks the site's own social share buttons (`sns-share-btn`), which leave an almost empty grey-share-icon band between the author card and the related-tags section. Adding `tour.ne.jp##.sns-share-btn` to the Social filter hid both share buttons with the page intact and no residue, confirmed by the browser experiment and vision review. ## Rule `tour.ne.jp##.sns-share-btn` ## Policy rationale The report is a social-widget leftover, which is neither first-party advertising, a paywall, nor a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. There is no anti-adblock wall on the page, so the anti-adblock gate does not apply. The AdGuard Social filter's stated purpose covers 'Share' buttons on third-party sites, and its exceptions (comments, embedded posts, polls, login widgets, links to the site's social pages) do not cover this share control. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d33bf95a3b5d74aedcc3e19163260eb82ba9a9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 8546](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d33bf95a3b5d74aedcc3e19163260eb82ba9a9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L8546). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On carpet-rug.org the Cookie Notices filter's generic rule #⁠#⁠#⁠gdpr-cookie-consent-bar hides the GDPR Cookie Consent bar, leaving the plugin's empty full-viewport modal plus black backdrop over the whole page so nothing can be clicked and the cookie-gated video never unlocks. A site-scoped trusted-click-element rule on #⁠cookie_action_accept_all removes that overlay and loads the YouTube player (phase-C viewport shows the player, page integrity intact, no ad residue), but the review rejected it only because tiled full-page captures paint every cross-origin YouTube iframe as a black rectangle, which I reproduced in an unfiltered browser.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"119d17e73a50ab35aef35208255882477e50d035b522c4203efc0389744394b6"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠246612 is a real leftover:⁠ five empty `div.ad-slot-root` gpt containers reserve 250px of blank space each on www⁠.ilfoglio.it because the ad scripts are already blocked. The proposed rule `ilfoglio.it##.ad-slot-root` was applied and removed all ad reservation with the page intact, but the vision review refused it for blank regions that measured checks prove are unloaded lazy article photos and a first-party "IL FOGLIO ON AIR" promo, not ad space, so it reaches a human unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Bottom viewport, over the three-teaser row beneath the Trump/Ukraine lead story — Floating dark 'IL FOGLIO ON AIR' / 'Il Foglio, ora anche video.' promotional banner with an ON AIR badge and a 'VAI AL PALINSESTO' button overlays article text at the bottom of the viewport; it is a visible special-banner/ad overlay, not blank space.
- Right-hand column below the article 'L’elzeviro di Fini:⁠ “La sinistra che festeggia per Trump, poi perde in Italia. È rimasta yankee go home”' — Large empty white reserved advertising region occupying the right column from below the Fini article to the bottom of the tile; no creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is visible inside it.
- Le false minacce sugli aerei ci ricordano che sulla cybersicurezza la politica non si può più dividere / Tajani:⁠ "Diffusi i miei dati personali sul dark web" — Large empty white reserved ad-slot region above this article teaser; no ad creative, label, frame, iframe, or placeholder block is visible inside it.
- L’ex presidente della Republika Srpska a Mar-a-Lago — right-hand side of the lead image — Large reserved white rectangle beside the Dodik article image; no ad creative, REKLAMA label, frame, or placeholder is rendered in it, consistent with an empty leftover ad slot.
- La notizia che non c’è:⁠ i cattolici non hanno votato Trump / I prossimi regali di Trump ai dem — right-hand column — Tall blank white column to the right of the bottom article list; no ad creative, label, frame, or placeholder is visible, consistent with leftover empty ad-slot area.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Full-page capture does not trigger loading="lazy" article images, so the vision review reads their reserved boxes as leftover ad space: On www⁠.ilfoglio.it (1920x19961 page) 45 of 46 article images carry loading="lazy". In the live session only 6 image requests were made (artifact:⁠har:⁠76e31611-af1f-42a3-bc1b-2b7a5eec37bd), and evaluate_js reports 40 lazy <⁠img⁠> elements not yet loaded reserving \~14,656 px of box height, none of them inside an ad slot; 39 of the 46 images were also incomplete at the time of the first full-page capture. The apply_rule full-page tiles therefore show large white rectangles in article columns, and both vision reviews classified them as "large empty white reserved ad regions" (and once as "non-target rendering damage"). Scrolling the page in interact_page reduces the incomplete count only slightly, and the tiled capture itself never forces those images to load. What is missing is a capture mode (or a required reveal step) that forces lazy resources to load before the full-page capture, so a "blank space" that is really an unloaded article photo is not scored as an ad leftover or as page damage.

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report's premise is real:⁠ AdGuard Base filter ships 12 facebook.com-scoped `#%#` JS rules, including the sponsored-post MutationObserver rule the reporter quotes, applied on every facebook.com load. The reported defect is main-thread jank on a logged-in feed, which this run could not reach (both facebook.com URLs showed a sign-in wall) and which no filter-list rule can fix, so a maintainer rewrite of those rule bodies is needed; the only filter-expressible lever is carried, not endorsed.

## Candidate for review

BaseFilter/sections/allowlist.txt

Not verified: Carried for a human decision, not endorsed. The symptom is a main-thread timing defect on a logged-in Facebook feed; this run reached only a sign-in wall on two facebook.com URLs (full-page vision:⁠ sign_in_wall, reporterSymptomPresence indeterminate, instanceCount 0), so the \~10.4 s observer cost and the candidate's effect on it could not be measured, and apply_rule's screenshot phases cannot judge timing. The rule is a domain-wide unblock:⁠ 12 Base-filter `#%#` rules are scoped to facebook.com (sponsored feed posts, complementary sidebar, watch, marketplace), so this exception disables all of them and brings those ads back, against the policy that unblocking rules be as specific as possible; no `$jsinject` rule exists in this repository, so the path is a guess. The real fix is a maintainer rewrite of the existing `#%#` rule bodies, which no filter-list rule can express.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Run instruction has no policy for reports about performance cost of existing filter rules: The run instruction's filter policy lists close/no-rule cases (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, other anti-adblock without a captured detector) and maintainer rules for anti-adblock popups and shared rules, but says nothing about a report whose defect is the runtime performance cost of already-shipped filter rules (here:⁠ facebook.com `#%#` MutationObserver rules in Base filter). It is therefore undefined whether such a report should be closed, handed to a maintainer, or answered with an unblocking exception such as `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject`, and which of those the outcome type must express.

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's outlined defect on www⁠.tozlu.com is the site's own fixed cookie-consent card ("Çerez tercihleriniz" with accept/reject/settings), served in the page HTML with no consent-vendor request behind it. Hiding its stable component class with tozlu.com#⁠#⁠.ms-cerez-bandi verified in the A/B/C experiment (card visible in baseline, hidden with the candidate, page integrity intact, no remaining instances) and belongs in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `tozlu.com##.ms-cerez-bandi` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance, which belongs to an AdGuard annoyance filter; no policy rule in the run instruction closes it (it is not the site's first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall). The reporter-defined target is the site's own cookie-consent card, and the fix is a standard domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — mebelplyt.pl (PrestaShop shop using the first-party 'seigicookie' module built on the orestbida cookieconsent library) still shows its centered "Używamy ciasteczek!" consent dialog under the reporter's setup, whose Cookie Notices filter is enabled. The fix is to add mebelplyt.pl to the existing shared cookieconsent element-hiding rule `…,rsd.cz###cc_div` in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt; the domain-scoped form was validated with apply_rule (symptom resolved, page integrity intact). ## Rule `mebelplyt.pl###cc_div` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent annoyance, not first-party advertising, a paywall, an anti-adblock wall, or a scam/phishing page, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The reported element is a removable overlay whose serving request is visible (first-party /modules/seigicookie/…), and the fix belongs to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's existing shared cookieconsent rule family, which the run instruction says to extend rather than duplicate. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 7795](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L7795). ## Screenshots

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The site's first-party ad-block detector (忍者AdMax tag v1.0.0 in /js/lsf-support.js) did execute, but its bait and network probes are already neutralised by the existing ff14-tools.com rules in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt, and full-page vision of three successful loads shows the reported overlay absent, so closing as not reproduced is recommended.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's policy does not block a rule here:⁠ this is a non-German anti-adblock wall and the captured requests do show the detector script (first-party https:⁠//ff14-tools.com/js/lsf-support.js plus its adm.shinobi.jp/abd.js probes), so rule generation was permitted. The close recommendation rests on non-reproduction, not on a policy rule:⁠ the reported anti-adblock overlay was absent on every successful load of the reported URL with the reporter's filter selection, confirmed by session-bound full-page vision (reporterSymptomPresence absent).

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — dlh.pl serves a first-party cookie-consent modal that dims and locks the whole page; hiding it would leave the page dark and unscrollable, so the fix declines consent through the site's own cookie. The rule `dlh.pl#%#//scriptlet('trusted-set-cookie', 'cookieConsentPrefs', …)` was verified in the reporter's import profile — modal gone, no remaining instances, page integrity intact. ## Rule `dlh.pl#%#//scriptlet('trusted-set-cookie', 'cookieConsentPrefs', '{%22cg_essential%22:1%2C%22cg_marketing%22:0%2C%22cg_functionality%22:0%2C%22cg_statistical%22:0%2C%22expire%22:182%2C%22secure%22:true}')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent annoyance on a Polish site, not first-party advertising, a paywall or a German anti-adblock wall, so no closing rule of the run instruction applies. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is the filter whose stated purpose covers cookie notices and CMP requests, and its policy allows declining non-essential cookies by default, which is what this rule does. The consent mechanism is first-party (window.__idea07PrivacyConsentCfg, consent_cookie_name cookieConsentPrefs); no third-party vendor script exists to block, so the Cookie Notices filter's alternative consent method applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 1030](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L1030). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter-defined annoyance on drewmax-online.pl is the bottom-fixed cookie-consent banner "Polityka Prywatności" (AKCEPTUJ WSZYSTKIE PLIKI COOKIES / AKCEPTUJ TYLKO NIEZBĘDNE), reproduced live, and the fix is adding drewmax-online.pl to the existing shared rule ...#⁠#⁠.cookie-notice-ui in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"12c6a777b1511f8d9dd0ac2127d61f56fddfd382509afa1aeff52c85239068d2"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported banner above the yandex.ru video player is a Yandex-owned product promotion («Яндекс Книги», labelled «РЕКЛАМА») delivered from Yandex's own ad host on Yandex's own site, so the repository policy for the site's own advertising says no rule is needed; the overlay also never rendered in the live session (all Direct slots were 0×0 and the video itself is unplayable there), so no rule could have been validated anyway. Recommending closing rather than adding a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The defect defined by the reporter screenshot is a banner labelled «РЕКЛАМА» that advertises «Яндекс Книги» — a Yandex-owned service — immediately above the video player on Yandex's own video page (yandex.ru/video/preview/12475870074233340135). Knowledge Base filter policy (Ad blocking filters — Limitations and exceptions):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." The same rule bars deliberately adding a rule for this placement. Live evidence agrees on provenance:⁠ the page's ad inventory is delivered from Yandex's own ad host yandex-video.naydex.net (53 requests, all HTTP 200, none blocked by the reporter's lists) on Yandex's own property, and the page's Direct placements were present but unfilled, so no third-party creative was observed that would fall outside the first-party rule.

## Artifacts

Not anti-adblock at all and not a scam/phishing page, so the report is handled like any other and the cookie-notice rule may be written. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — rybnet.pl shows its first-party "Pliki cookies" consent dialog over a full-screen dark backdrop that blocks the page; the only filter rule acting there was a generic `###cookieFooter` one. The verified fix is `rybnet.pl#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#ab-deny')`, which presses the site's own "Nie akceptuję" button so the module removes both the dialog and the overlay, and belongs in the AdGuard Cookie Notices section file cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `rybnet.pl#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#ab-deny')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a cookie-consent notice, which belongs to AdGuard Cookie Notices (Annoyances) — none of the run instruction's no-rule categories apply:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German/other anti-adblock wall (the page never asks to disable the ad blocker and no detector script appears in the captured requests). The page's own script is a first-party consent module with its own decline handler, so a filter rule is the right fix and no maintainer hand-off condition applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — gfiber.com serves a first-party "Your privacy choices" cookie-consent MUI dialog that covers the page and locks body scrolling (reporter screenshot 1). A trusted-click-element scriptlet that triggers the dialog's own close button was verified in the reporter profile:⁠ the dialog disappears and the page's overlay/scroll state returns to normal. ## Rule `gfiber.com#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.styles_dialog__eycoV button[aria-label="close"]', '', '1000')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a first-party cookie consent notice (annoyance), which the run instruction's policy does not close:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall (the page shows no ad-blocker detection and no anti-adblock request was captured). The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists precisely for this class of rule (AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections), so generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - trusted-click-element scriptlet signature not documented in the served guidance: The lookup_rule_guidance 'scriptlet' topic returned only general scriptlet/trusted-scriptlet compatibility text and no argument reference for trusted-click-element (selector, extraMatch/containsText, delay semantics, whether it waits for the element to appear). The candidate rule relies on repository precedent from search_rules results, e.g. AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 143:⁠ '...#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.if6_eprivacy a[⁠data-form=".eprivacy_optin_decline"]⁠', '', '3500')'. An explicit parameter reference would remove that uncertainty. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — picme.pl shows a full-screen Real Cookie Banner consent overlay (div[⁠consent-skip-blocker]⁠ holding the 'Preferencje dot. prywatności' dialog); the picme.pl-scoped form of the repository's existing shared Real Cookie Banner rule removes it, verified in the reporter's extension profile with page integrity intact. ## Rule `picme.pl#$?#div[consent-skip-blocker] { remove: true; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported problem is a cookie/consent notice, not first-party advertising, a paywall or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's close rules applies. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block cookie notices and CMP requests, and policy states hiding the notice is normally sufficient and non-essential cookies are declined by default. The rule belongs to an existing shared multi-domain Real Cookie Banner rule, so the host merges the picme.pl-scoped candidate into that rule instead of a new duplicate. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 365](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L365). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — apkvision.org shows an empty 250px AdSense wrapper (`div.adsbox.apk-post-adsense`, empty `ins.adsbygoogle`) between the recommendation carousel and Comments — the blank area the reporter boxed. Hiding it removed 278px of blank space with page integrity intact and no observed damage, but the vision review kept rejecting the small remaining section spacing, so the rule stays unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`apkvision.org##.apk-post-adsense`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule ran twice on the locked CLI baseline. The candidate rule hid the target in both (adElementStatus visible→hidden, document height 3765→3487, pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty, failedCandidateChecks empty, environmentExperiment inconclusive), and domChecks on the second run measured the space the review named:⁠ gap between the carousel and the Comments section 306px→28px, the adsbox 250px→0 with display:⁠none, and zero visible elements left in that band — i.e. only the comments section's own 28px margin remains. The dedicated vision review nevertheless returned verdict 'rejected' with symptom 'not_resolved', adLayoutResidue 'present' and two remaining instances describing a '\~300px' blank gap, which the measured DOM contradicts. A semantically broader second candidate (apkvision.org#⁠#⁠.adsbox) produced the same verdict. CSS injection was not permitted because ordinary #⁠#⁠ hiding showed no page-integrity regression and no scroll-lock failure.

## Still visible after the rule

- Between the game recommendation carousel and the Comments section — A large blank white reserved gap is visible below the Minecraft/Getting Over It/Incredibox recommendation carousel and above the Comments header. No ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is visible in the gap; it is empty reserved advertising space.
- Document y=1956..2768; between the Similar/Popular/Hot recommendation carousel and the Comments heading — A visibly empty reserved gap sits directly below the game recommendation carousel and above the Comments section. No ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder text is visible in this blank area.

Indeterminate — Reproduced the AirlineGeeks anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page's Advanced Ads Pro extended-adblocker opens `<dialog id="modal-extended-adblocker">` over a dimmed article and has no close control. `airlinegeeks.com,thedesk.net,dairybusinessmea.com,readhunters.xyz###modal-extended-adblocker`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on www⁠.sideproject.games is the site's WordPress "Age Gate" overlay, which covers the review article and, through `html.age-gate__restricted`/`body.age-restriction`, clips the page to one screen so the article is unreadable. A domain-scoped CSS-injection rule that hides the overlay via the plugin's own `--ag-form-display` variable and restores height/overflow on the restricted html/body was verified with the reporter's filter profile:⁠ gate gone, article text and media readable, page integrity intact. ## Rule `sideproject.games#$#.age-gate__wrapper, html.age-gate__restricted, body.age-restriction { --ag-form-display: none !important; height: auto !important; overflow: visible !important; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ this is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall at all — the page shows the site's own age-verification popup, so no close/hand-off rule applies. KB filter policy, AdGuard Popups filter:⁠ it blocks popups 'not necessary for normal site usage', including 'other types of popups that may annoy users (at the discretion of filter developers)'; the restriction it forbids concerns circumventing content access measures that ask the user to pay, which this gate does not do. Repository precedent:⁠ the same class family is already handled per site (`thegrowthop.com##.age-gate-wrapper` in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt). Candidate validated:⁠ apply_rule environmentExperiment verified, visual review verified, symptom resolved, no remaining instances, page integrity intact, no observed damage. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7dd228bb7a0b292537d62795234bd12a4063e477/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42481886819 Automated analysis against filters at `7dd228b`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.cwtv.com/channels/ shows an Admiral (VRM) anti-adblock gate over the live-channel player that also locks page scrolling via inline overflow:⁠hidden on html/body. Hiding the gate alone left the page unscrollable, so the verified fix is one domain-scoped CSS-injection rule that both hides the Admiral overlay and releases the scroll lock. ## Rule `cwtv.com#$#html, body, div.fEy1Z2XT { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction, anti-adblock policy:⁠ a non-German anti-adblock wall may be fixed once the captured requests show the detector script. The captured requests contain the Admiral detector loader https:⁠//honeybutterbliss.com/v2ptcFRTBpffYOcFbdmGik-g-7ITe1HsbbnamSV0VMaoCkguHH7na_NzYoThow0ZW (script, third-party, 200), inserted by the page's inline 'Admiral Visitor Relationship Management Tag for cwtv.com', and the wall markup links to percent-encoded getadmiral.com. The wall aggressively demands disabling the ad blocker ('DISABLE MY ADBLOCKER', 'Please add CWTV to your ad blocker's allow list') and overlays the player plus locks page scrolling, so it is an anti-adblock wall the filter policy permits blocking. Not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German-language site wall, so none of the policy carve-outs apply. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7dd228bb7a0b292537d62795234bd12a4063e477/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 12033](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7dd228bb7a0b292537d62795234bd12a4063e477/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L12033). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's "support widget" on www⁠.mercedes-benz.com.tr is the site's fixed circular online-contact button (`.ocm-floating-cta`) overlapping the page copy; a domain-scoped element-hiding rule in the Widgets filter removes it, and the A/B experiment verified the widget gone with page integrity intact. ## Rule `mercedes-benz.com.tr##.ocm-floating-cta` ## Policy rationale The report is a support/chat widget annoyance (label T:⁠ Annoyance, comment 'support widget'), not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the policy rules that recommend closing applies. The site's floating contact/chat widget matches the AdGuard Widgets filter purpose:⁠ 'Chat widgets that are not integrated with the content and are not the main content of the page' / live support chats. No geographic proxy is required and the reported page loaded successfully (HTTP 200), so the symptom could be observed and validated live. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7dd228bb7a0b292537d62795234bd12a4063e477/AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
